paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. When life looks unfair, it's easy to say what these people said: "It is futile to serve God." They watched the arrogant prosper and decided that obeying God got them nothing (Malachi 3:14-15). I get it. But the LORD heard every word, and what He did next matters most (Malachi 3:13).

Because while some were complaining, others were talking with one another, and "the LORD listened and heard them." A scroll of remembrance was written for those who feared Him and honored His name (Malachi 3:16). He calls them His "treasured possession" and says He will spare them "as a man spares his own son who serves him" (Malachi 3:17). TREASURED, friend. Your faithfulness is never wasted, and it is never unseen.

The unfair stretch is not the end of the story. The LORD says a day is coming that will make the difference between the righteous and the wicked plain again (Malachi 3:18; 4:1-2). For those who fear His name, "the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings" (Malachi 4:2). That's why He says to remember His law and points to the great and awesome Day of the LORD (Malachi 4:4-5). So keep serving, friend, and keep those ovens ready.
